Hello, Product Hunt 🙌🏻 I'm Daniil, a software engineer. Today I'm launching \\Burrow\\: free, open-source virtual machines for Apple silicon Macs. \\🧩 Why I built it\\ I needed Linux, Windows and a clean macOS on my Mac, and I didn't want to pay for a Parallels license. So I built the tool I wanted: click \\+\\, pick a system, done. \\📦 What is Burrow?\\ A native SwiftUI app built on Apple's Virtualization.framework, plus `burrowctl`, a CLI for running the same machines headless. Everything runs locally, it's MIT licensed, and there's no account. \\🔑 Key features\\ - \\No ISO hunting:\\ Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian and Alpine are downloaded straight from each publisher and verified against SHA-256 - \\Windows 11 on ARM:\\ Setup runs unattended, with no TPM or Secure Boot checks and a local [...] Subscribe

📌 [...] unattended, with no TPM or Secure Boot checks and a local account; drivers install automatically \\⚙️ Under the hood\\ Linux and macOS run on Virtualization.framework. Windows runs on QEMU with Hypervisor.framework, because the Windows boot manager hangs under Virtualization.framework. I also patched QEMU for a 60 fps display. \\🚧 Honest limitations\\ ARM64 guests only. Windows has no vTPM or 3D acceleration yet, and there's no USB passthrough. PRs are very welcome; these are great first contributions. \\🙏 Your feedback\\ What would make you drop Parallels or UTM for this? Bug reports, feature requests and ⭐ on GitHub all help a lot. 👉  Best, Daniil
